analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow patches, their continuation, and BASE lines 1–518. .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml now disables visible Actions cache restores/saves on darkbloom-* runners without DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL (HEAD 63–75 and repeated job setup), including fixture and cluster metadata caches. Fixture preparation and security-related test execution retain their existing conditions; disabling caching does not itself bypass those tests. Restored .git validation now rejects symlinks, active hooks and selected executable/include configuration before rev-parse/fsck (HEAD 106–131, repeated across seven jobs), improving on BASE 92–98. Potential broader cache-poisoning weaknesses are not established as new regressions by this change.
The changes affect CI build integrity and availability, relevant to A-017/A-018 and T-054, not serving authorization, billing, coordinator/provider encryption or prompt storage. T-041 concerns inference KV caches, not these CI caches; its cryptographic and tenant-scoping controls are unchanged in the supplied evidence. No supported security regression was identified.
Integration should verify that .github/actions/provider-ci-build, invoked at BASE 115/194, honors CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off for its nested cache operations, and reconcile the runner provisioning contract that supplies RUNNER_NAME and DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. This workflow only detects endpoint presence; it does not configure or authenticate cache redirection itself. Those directly relevant implementations were not supplied, so the stated prevention of GitHub-cache fallback remains unverified rather than a finding. Scope is bounded workflow evidence, not a full audit or qualification review.
